size_ratchet.unzipped_ceiling_why: AWS Lambda refuses to unpack a deployment package above 250 MB.
enforced_in: the builder, which deletes the zip and its sidecar and exits 2 rather than leave an unuploadable artefact behind
scripts/deploy/bundle_manifest.py, which measures the finished file
size_ratchet.proved_by: python scripts/deploy/bundle_manifest.py out/lambda/mainline-demo-api-arm64.zip --quiet --max-zipped-mb 1 -> REFUSED [SIZE] zipped 7989296 bytes exceeds the Lambda ceiling of 1048576 bytes, exit 2

determinism.claim: Two builds of the same tree produce the same sha256, on either shell, into any output directory.
how: every ZipInfo.date_time is (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0), the DOS epoch
entries are written in sorted order of the UTF-8 bytes of their relative path
external_attr is 0o755 for shared objects and 0o644 for everything else, create_system 3
no directory entries are written at all
pip runs with --no-compile, so no .pyc carries a source mtime, and wheels are installed from a wheelhouse with --no-index rather than re-resolved
determinism.verified_by: scripts/deploy/bundle_manifest.py --strict, which re-reads those six properties out of the finished zip's central directory

source_maps.why: A judge who opens DevTools on the demo should see component names and real stack frames, not surface-Bv8EMlU6.js:1:20481. This project's argument is that its claims are checkable; shipping an unreadable bundle to save bytes we are not short of would contradict it.
source_maps.escape_hatch: scripts/deploy/build_lambda.sh --strip-source-maps (-StripSourceMaps in PowerShell). It is the first thing to try if the 50 MB ratchet ever refuses.

caveats: NOT DEPLOYED. This records a built artefact, not a running function. `terraform apply` was not run by this worker and is not this worker's to run (docs/leads/ship-final.md section 2.2).

The console dist/ in this package carries NEITHER VITE_MAINLINE_API_BASE NOR VITE_MAINLINE_BUNDLE_URL: it was built as a plain `vite build` (import.meta.env MODE=production) rather than `vite build --mode demo`. The site loads, the SPA mounts, and every surface then renders its NO SOURCE panel, because src/app/source-select.ts selects a transport purely from those two build-time variables. The bundle is therefore a working website with no data source. dist/ is not this worker's file; the builder prints the exact rebuild command as a WARNING on every run and records the probe in the sidecar manifest under `console`.

The reproducibility claim is same-machine, same-tree, both shells, three builds. It is NOT a claim that a different OS or a different pip would resolve the same wheels: the wheel sha256s are recorded here precisely so that a rebuild elsewhere can be compared rather than assumed.
dist/.vite/manifest.json is shipped because it is part of dist/. It is Vite's build map, it names only chunk files that are already public in the package, and nothing requests it at runtime.
verdict: BUILT AND REPRODUCIBLE. Two architectures, three builds each across two shells, byte-identical per architecture. Both packages contain mainline_demo_api/, psycopg/, web/index.html and web/bundle/, are far inside both Lambda size ceilings, and serve / and /bundle/* through the handler that will run them.
